conversation_binding.why_the_binding_lives_on_the_reach_mode: The refs at profile scope name the conversation vendor and the carrier as two separate companies, inherited from an era when they were. A vendor that supplies both then has nowhere correct to be named. Reach modes differ in exactly this way, so the party that carries the call and the party that runs the speaking side belong to the mode, not to the profile.
conversation_binding.the_two_refs_above_may_be_the_same_conne: That is the point. AgentPhone carries the call AND runs the speaking side, so both resolve to one record. Requiring them to differ is what made a single-vendor route unrepresentable.
conversation_binding.what_the_speaking_profile_is_and_is_not: A handle at the carrier, nothing more. This id is the vendor's untouched starter agent, sitting in their `hosted` voice mode with their website demo script as its prompt, and that is FINE for an outbound call: the outbound request carries its own `systemPrompt`, and when it does the vendor runs the LLM against OUR wording regardless of the agent's inbound configuration. The agent's own prompt never reaches the call.
conversation_binding.this_field_was_null_for_four_hours_and_t: It read: 'naming that id here would make every ref resolve and put a demo bot on a real call.' That is false for outbound and it made a live record teach a blocker that did not exist. It is the same defect as the NOT_RUN verdict corrected in the sibling engine profile on the same day: a field that reads as impossible when it is merely unconfigured. The account state behind the claim was verified and correct; the conclusion drawn from it was not checked against the vendor's outbound semantics.
conversation_binding.why_turn_delivery_is_null_and_why_that_d: Webhook mode needs a publicly reachable route that receives caller speech and returns what to say, and none is declared in this package, in service-connections, or in the carrier note. That is a real gap for INBOUND turns and for the target architecture where the model is ours too. It is not required to place an outbound call, because an outbound call with a `systemPrompt` is answered hosted-side.
conversation_binding.reading_the_result_back_needs_no_webhook: Verified 2026-09-04 against the vendor's published API. The transcript is retrievable by exchange id, so nothing has to be pushed to us, and `service-connections` ALREADY declares the operation: `read_exchange`, GET https://api.agentphone.ai/v1/calls/{exchange_ref}, which returns the call detail with its ordered transcript. Poll it until the status is terminal. An agent reading only the null above would conclude the outcome is unreadable and go build a receiver, which is work that is already done one package over. The vendor also exposes a dedicated transcript sub-resource and an SSE stream for in-flight turns; neither is added here, because `read_exchange` already returns the transcript and a second endpoint for the same fact would be a duplicate owner.
conversation_binding.why_hosted_outbound_is_not_the_bland_rej: Bland was rejected because the model, the wording AND the live transcript all belonged to it. Here the wording is ours through the per-call prompt, and the transcript is read back by us through the already-declared `read_exchange` operation rather than pushed to us by an event we have no receiver for. Only the model is theirs. That is a real difference and it is still not the destination: webhook mode remains the target so the model is ours too.
conversation_binding.why_those_two_are_superseded: Telnyx reached self-serve trial, was disabled after two declined card attempts on an empty bound account, and its calls end at call.start.error-get-transport. Vapi's own numbers are capped at zero outbound, so it needs an imported carrier number and the only proven one was Telnyx. They stay named because a dead ref deleted without trace reads as a ref that never existed, and the next agent re-shops the same vendor.

reach_modes.why_proof_status_did_not_move: Repointing refs is not proof that a call connects. Only ONE null remains, `turn_delivery_ref`, and it blocks inbound turns rather than an outbound call or its readback. This once said `two nulls`, which stopped being true when `remote_speaking_profile_ref` was filled, and a stale count is exactly the kind of leftover that makes a record read as more blocked than it is. The status stays NOT_RUN for the only honest reason left: no call has been placed yet. Marking it otherwise would be the overclaim this correction exists to catch.
